NO. 063 · Coast & Tidal Flats / Laridae · Gulls & Terns

Saunders's Gull

黑嘴鸥 · hēi zuǐ ōu Saundersilarus saundersi
Winter visitor Locally common 29–32 cm Protected (Class I) IUCN VU

China's own rare little gull — fewer than twenty thousand left

One of the few gulls centred on China: it breeds in the Bohai Bay and winters on the south-east coast, and the world population is only about ten thousand birds. A short black bill, a dark smudge behind the ear in winter, red legs — meeting one on a Zhuhai mudflat is worth writing down.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillBlack, short and stout for a gull — the origin of the name.
  • HeadEntirely black in breeding condition; in non-breeding dress, which is what we see in a South China winter, the head is white with a distinct black crescent behind the ear.
  • PlumageBack and wings pale grey, underparts white, wingtips black; in flight the underwing is pale grey with obvious black tips.
  • LegsRed to orange-red, in sharp contrast with the black bill.

Behaviour

It feeds on mudflats and in shallow estuary water, by snatching from the surface, pecking in the shallows and picking along the tide line. It often mixes with other gulls and waders. Demanding about habitat, it depends heavily on coastal mudflats and fish ponds, so reclamation and disturbance are the main threats. There are regular wintering records on the Zhuhai coast; observe at low tide, from a distance, at the edge of the mudflat.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Jinwan tidal flats
  • Qi'ao Island outer flats
  • Hengqin estuary
  • Doumen coastal fish ponds
Field note
A nationally protected species (Class I). Separating it from Black-headed Gull: Saunders's has a black bill, is smaller and has redder legs; Black-headed has a bright red bill and legs, is larger, and its winter ear-spot is more diffuse.
